hook: Fifteen questions, no second chances. Can you score fifteen out of fifteen? Let us find out.

questions.question: Who is credited with inventing the World Wide Web?
questions.question_speech: Question one. Who is credited with inventing the World Wide Web? A. Bill Gates. B. Steve Jobs. C. Tim Berners-Lee. D. Mark Zuckerberg.

questions.question: What does CPU stand for?
questions.question_speech: Question two. What does CPU stand for? A. Central Processing Unit. B. Computer Power Unit. C. Central Program Utility. D. Core Processing Unit.
questions.answer_speech: A is correct, Central Processing Unit.

questions.question: What does USB stand for?
questions.question_speech: Question three. What does USB stand for? A. Universal Serial Bus. B. United System Board. C. Unified Signal Box. D. Universal Storage Base.
questions.answer_speech: A is correct, Universal Serial Bus.

questions.question: Which company created the iPhone?
questions.question_speech: Question four. Which company created the iPhone? A. Samsung. B. Apple. C. Google. D. Nokia.

questions.question: Who invented the movable type printing press in Europe?
questions.question_speech: Question five. Who invented the movable type printing press in Europe? A. Leonardo da Vinci. B. Isaac Newton. C. Johannes Gutenberg. D. Galileo.

questions.question: Which number system do computers use?
questions.question_speech: Question six. Which number system do computers use? A. Decimal. B. Roman. C. Hexagonal. D. Binary.

questions.question: Who made the first successful powered airplane flight in 1903?
questions.question_speech: Question seven. Who made the first successful powered airplane flight in 1903? A. The Wright brothers. B. The Montgolfier brothers. C. Charles Lindbergh. D. Amelia Earhart.
questions.answer_speech: A is correct, the Wright brothers.

questions.question: What does GPS stand for?
questions.question_speech: Question eight. What does GPS stand for? A. General Position System. B. Global Positioning System. C. Great Path Sensor. D. Global Planet Signal.
questions.answer_speech: B is correct, Global Positioning System.

questions.question: Who discovered penicillin?
questions.question_speech: Question nine. Who discovered penicillin? A. Louis Pasteur. B. Marie Curie. C. Alexander Fleming. D. Edward Jenner.

questions.question: What does AI stand for?
questions.question_speech: Question ten. What does AI stand for? A. Artificial Intelligence. B. Automatic Internet. C. Advanced Input. D. Applied Interface.

questions.question: What was the name of the first artificial satellite launched in 1957?
questions.question_speech: Question eleven. What was the name of the first artificial satellite launched in 1957? A. Explorer One. B. Apollo. C. Sputnik One. D. Vostok.

questions.question: What does RAM stand for in a computer?
questions.question_speech: Question twelve. What does RAM stand for in a computer? A. Read Any Memory. B. Random Access Memory. C. Rapid Active Module. D. Run All Memory.
questions.answer_speech: B is correct, Random Access Memory.

questions.question: What does PDF stand for?
questions.question_speech: Question thirteen. What does PDF stand for? A. Portable Document Format. B. Printed Data File. C. Personal Document Folder. D. Public Data Format.
questions.answer_speech: A is correct, Portable Document Format.

questions.question: Who is credited with patenting the first practical telephone in 1876?
questions.question_speech: Question fourteen. Who is credited with patenting the first practical telephone in 1876? A. Thomas Edison. B. Nikola Tesla. C. Alexander Graham Bell. D. Guglielmo Marconi.
questions.answer_speech: C is correct, Alexander Graham Bell.

questions.question: What does Wi-Fi allow devices to do?
questions.question_speech: Question fifteen. What does Wi-Fi allow devices to do? A. Charge wirelessly. B. Connect to a network wirelessly. C. Print in color. D. Store data offline.
questions.answer_speech: B is correct, connect to a network wirelessly.
